commons.title: Tribute to Bidai Tribe in Huntsville, Texas.jpg
commons.description: This tribute to the Bidai tribe is in a wooded area called Founders Park in Huntsville, Texas.  Huntsville is thought to be a trading location for several tribes, but the Bidai were local.
commons.editorial_reason: The image is a Bidai tribute, specifically another people, despite the Atakapa source category.

commons.title: Sketches of 8 Native Americans and 1 African in New Orleans 1735 by Alexandre de Batz.jpg
commons.description: A watercolor sketch of 8 Native Americans of various tribes and 1 boy of African descent in 1735. The Native American on the far right with the pipe is Atakapa. The French depended on Native Americans and imported Africans for labour. Made by the French artist Alexander de Batz (1685-1759). The caption in the top left is in French "Desseins de Sauvages de Plusieurs Nations, Nlle Orléans 1735." (Sketches of Savages of Several Nations, New Orleans 1735).
commons.editorial_reason: The description specifically identifies the far-right Native American as Atakapa, and the image visibly shows Indigenous dress and adornment.

commons.title: Nelumbo lutea.jpg
commons.description: The American lotus (Nelumbo lutea) is sometimes mistaken for a water lily, but it has two main differences. One is the seed pod, which is shaped a bit like a space capsule. The other difference is the leaf shape. Water lilies are not completely round; they have a slit. The American Lotus has big round (or roundish) leaves with no slit. Some are a foot across.
commons.editorial_reason: This is a generic American lotus photograph with no Atakapa cultural attribution.

commons.title: FEMA - 7053 - Photograph by Bob McMillan taken on 10-07-2002 in Louisiana.jpg
commons.description: Point-Aux-Chenes, LA, October 7, 2002 -- This small fishing community was hit hard by a seven foot tidal surge that accompanied Hurricane Lili.  Several homes in this community are elevated and did not receive the damage that the other homes did.    Photo by Bob McMillan/ FEMA News Photo
commons.editorial_reason: This shows a modern Louisiana fishing community and storm damage, with no specific Atakapa cultural link.
